subject.title: Slack button interactions should dispatch a reply turn, not a heartbeat wake (follow-up to #99544)

question: Should Slack reply button/select clicks remain heartbeat-owned system events, or should Slack synthesize normal inbound reply turns for user-initiated controls?
rationale: Current source proves the path is still heartbeat-owned, but changing it replaces a recently accepted Slack system-event design and must preserve plugin interactive handlers, native approvals, thread routing, and the related session-conflict recovery boundary.

options.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
options.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input and require tests plus live Slack proof for value, thread delivery, and busy-run behavior.

options.title: Keep Heartbeat And Harden It
options.body: Retain the system-event heartbeat design but require end-to-end proof that values, visible replies, and retry behavior are reliable.

options.title: Wait For Shared Conflict Review
options.body: Defer the delivery-owner choice until the related session-init conflict work is reviewed, then retest Slack interactions against the chosen recovery layer.

recommendation.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
recommendation.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input and require tests plus live Slack proof for value, thread delivery, and busy-run behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He made the predecessor closure decision around reply assembly and is the best evidenced owner for deciding whether that design should remain heartbeat-owned.
